answer.rationale: Write-path p99 has been climbing through a known settlement peak with heavy writes, which matches prior surge saturation (b3) better than an unindicated regional fault or a fail-closed dependency. Circuit breaking would shed customer writes and violate the objective; read-replica routing previously helped report/read offload, not settlement writes; failover mid-peak risks in-flight writes. The same-day release is a real competing cause, so b1 is being verified before any rollback, but the single intervention that keeps writes accepted now is adding headroom—useful for genuine peak load and for a only-moderately heavier build until a later window. Downstream settlement value is already at risk from 5x write latency, which is why write-shedding options are rejected. Cause remains uncertain.
